name: Upscale B2B
what: Runs done-for-you outbound sales campaigns (email, calls, LinkedIn) for B2B companies (businesses that sell to other businesses), and sells the email inboxes those campaigns send from. TrustMRR lists it as "Upscale System LLC".
title: Upscale B2B sold $3 email inboxes to cold-email agencies, then became one, and now makes about $99K a month
dek: It started by selling the 'picks and shovels' of cold email (the tools everyone doing it needs): ready-to-send inboxes for a few dollars a month. Then it started running campaigns itself, with a free-to-try pilot. Its MRR (monthly recurring revenue: what customers pay every month) is $140,324, read straight from Stripe. That is higher than October's revenue, the money actually collected that month, so the two numbers don't match.
pattern: Sell the tools to people already in the game

first_revenue.text: Not public. By May 2025 the site was selling ready-to-send Google and Microsoft email inboxes from $2 to $7 a month each.
first_revenue.label: Wayback

first_customers.text: Not public. The 2025 site says it was 'specially built for Lead gen Agency Owners' who send cold email for their clients.

phases.name: Fixing their own problem
phases.story: Cold email means emailing businesses that don't know you yet. To send a lot without landing in spam, agencies (companies that do this work for clients) need many 'warmed up' inboxes: new inboxes used gently at first so email providers trust them. The company's site says it had been burned by bad inbox providers, 'That's why we started Upscale B2B'. TrustMRR lists March 2023 as the founding date.
phases.lesson: A problem that annoys you at work is often a problem other people will pay to make go away.

phases.name: Selling inboxes to agencies
phases.story: The site sold Google Workspace and Microsoft inboxes, set up and warmed, for $2 to $7 a month each, with a free domain (a web address). Bigger buyers got lower prices: $2.50 each at 100 inboxes, $2 at 1,000. A sales calculator showed how many deals more inboxes could bring.
phases.lesson: Selling to businesses that already spend money on a problem is easier than convincing someone they have one.

phases.name: A separate brand for inboxes
phases.story: The inbox business got its own site, warminboxes.com, first archived in April 2025 with 'Get FREE Warmed-Up Domains'. By November 2025 its headline promised '90%+ Deliverability' (the share of emails that land in the inbox, not spam). The founder's TrustMRR account is named after it.
phases.lesson: If one product sells itself, give it its own name and page so people can find it.

phases.name: Running campaigns, try first
phases.story: By January 2026 upscaleb2b.com led with done-for-you lead generation (finding possible customers for a business) and a trial: 'the only provider offering a trial for fully managed lead generation'. It runs a small pilot campaign first, then grows it if it works. Revenue went from about $34K in December 2025 to $99K in October 2026.
phases.lesson: Letting customers try before they commit can win clients who would never sign a big contract cold.

fact_checks.found: October 2026 revenue was $99,409. MRR counts what active subscriptions will pay each month now, so it can be higher than last month's revenue if new subscriptions started in November.

checklist: List 3 tools or supplies people in a hobby you know (gaming, sneakers, music) keep complaining about.
Find one group that already pays for something (like small video editors or club organisers) and ask what breaks most often.
Price one small product per unit, and write a cheaper price for people who buy 10 or more.
Offer a free 'pilot': one small piece of work for one customer, and agree first what 'it worked' means.
Make a simple calculator in Google Sheets that shows a customer what they'd get if they bought more.
Ask one happy customer for a one-sentence review you can put on your page.
